extraction_scope: Worker-6 conservative source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary XML/PDF figure captions, results, and methods; no figure pixel quantification was fabricated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: β2M antibacterial activity is potassium-buffer dependent in the primary MIC experiments; this is an activity-condition finding, not proof of direct membrane binding.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: β2-microglobulin purified from human amniotic fluid
mechanism_claims.limitations: Primary source explicitly states that these results do not confirm β2M binding to the cell membrane.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: β2M exposure is associated with dissipation of bacterial membrane potential in the DiSC3-5 assay, stronger for antibiotic-susceptible E. coli than the resistant strain in the reported experiment.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: E. coli ATCC 25922 and E. coli CCARM 1229 assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: Quantitative curve values were not recovered from local figure pixels; claim is limited to source-stated direction and assay type.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: β2M did not produce SYTOX green uptake even at multiples of the MIC in the reported E. coli assay, so membrane-potential dissipation should not be restated as gross membrane permeabilization.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: E. coli ATCC 25922 SYTOX green assay
mechanism_claims.limitations: Negative permeability result is source-supported; no exact fluorescence values were extracted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LPS stimulation of WISH amniotic epithelial cells increased β2M mRNA/protein in the paper, supporting host-response context rather than a direct antimicrobial mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: WISH amniotic epithelial cell expression assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: Expression response is contextual and is not used as MIC or direct bacterial killing evidence.
